# Proverbs 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A gentle reply defuses anger, but a cutting remark makes it explode.

**2** Wise people make knowledge attractive, but fools spew out nonsense.

**3** The LORD's eyes see everything — every place, every person, whether they're doing good or evil.

**4** Words that heal are a tree of life, but a twisted tongue crushes the spirit.

**5** Only a fool ignores their father's correction. Accepting it is the mark of a smart person.

**6** The home of a righteous person holds real treasure, but the wicked person's income brings nothing but problems.

**7** Wise people share knowledge wherever they go, but the hearts of fools have nothing worthwhile to offer.

**8** The LORD is disgusted by the religious rituals of wicked people, but He takes real pleasure in the prayers of the honest.

**9** The LORD hates the way wicked people live, but He loves anyone who pursues what's right.

**10** Harsh punishment awaits those who abandon the right path, and anyone who refuses correction will die.

**11** If even the realm of the dead is an open book to the LORD, how much more the thoughts inside every human heart!

**12** A mocker doesn't want to be corrected — that's why they never go to wise people for advice.

**13** A happy heart shows on your face, but a broken heart crushes your spirit.

**14** An understanding person looks for knowledge, but a fool's appetite is for more foolishness.

**15** For someone in constant pain, every day is miserable. But a cheerful heart makes life a continuous celebration.

**16** Better to have just a little and honor God than to have great wealth with anxiety attached.

**17** A simple meal served with love beats a gourmet dinner served with resentment.

**18** A hothead starts fights, but a patient person calms things down.

**19** A lazy person's road is like pushing through a thorn hedge, but the path of the upright is a clear highway.

**20** A wise child brings joy to a father, but a foolish person treats their mother with contempt.

**21** A senseless person finds foolishness entertaining, but someone with real understanding stays on course.

**22** Plans fall apart without good advice, but with plenty of counselors they hold together.

**23** There's real satisfaction in giving the right answer, and a word spoken at just the right moment — what a gift!

**24** The wise person's path leads upward toward life, steering them away from the grave below.

**25** The LORD demolishes the proud person's mansion but protects the widow's property line.

**26** The LORD finds evil schemes repulsive, but kind and honest words are pure in His sight.

**27** Chasing dishonest money brings ruin to your whole family, but refusing bribes keeps you alive.

**28** A righteous person thinks carefully before speaking, but a wicked person's mouth is a fire hose of harmful words.

**29** The LORD keeps His distance from wicked people, but He's close enough to hear when the righteous pray.

**30** Bright eyes make the heart glad, and good news gives strength to the whole body.

**31** If you can accept life-giving correction, you'll be right at home among wise people.

**32** Reject discipline and you're rejecting yourself. Accept correction and you gain wisdom.

**33** Wisdom begins with honoring the LORD, and humility paves the way for honor.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **15:1**: This might be the most practical verse in the entire Bible for everyday life. A calm response can stop a conflict in its tracks.

- **15:16-17**: Two of the most countercultural verses in any era — they say that peace, love, and contentment are worth more than any amount of money. And they're right.

- **15:23**: The right word at the right time is one of the greatest gifts one person can give another. Timing transforms good advice into something beautiful.

— PNEUMA
